title: NARRATIVE/SEQUENCE OF EVENTS
text:
At approximately 15:30 hours on March 15, 2024, I responded to a two-vehicle traffic collision at the
intersection of Main Street and First Avenue.
Investigation Summary: Vehicle #1 (Smith) was traveling southbound on Main Street in the right lane,
approaching the intersection with First Avenue. The traffic signal was red, and Vehicle #1 came to a
complete stop behind two other vehicles waiting at the light.
Vehicle #2 (Johnson) was also traveling southbound on Main Street in the same lane, approximately 50
feet behind Vehicle #1. According to witness statements and physical evidence, Vehicle #2 failed to brake
in time and struck the rear of Vehicle #1 while Vehicle #1 was lawfully stopped.
Impact Details:
Vehicle #2 struck Vehicle #1 at approximately 25-30 mph
Point of impact: Center rear of Vehicle #1
Vehicle #1 was pushed forward approximately 15 feet into the intersection
No contact with other vehicles or fixed objects
Driver Statements:
Smith (Vehicle #1): "I was stopped at the red light when I felt a huge impact from behind. I saw the light
was still red and there were cars in front of me, so I was completely stopped. I felt immediate pain in my
back and neck."
Johnson (Vehicle #2): "I was looking at my phone to check a text message when I looked up and saw
the cars stopped. I tried to brake but couldn't stop in time. I know I shouldn't have been on my phone
while driving."

title: WITNESS INFORMATION
text:
Witness #1: Maria Rodriguez
Address: 234 Elm Street, Springfield, CA 90210
Phone: (555) 321-6547
Statement: "I was in the left turn lane waiting for the light. I saw the blue Honda stopped normally at the
red light. Then I saw the silver Toyota coming fast and not slowing down. The driver looked like she was
looking down at something in her lap right before the crash."
Witness #2: Robert Chen
Address: 567 Maple Drive, Springfield, CA 90212
Phone: (555) 654-3210
Statement: "I was the car directly in front of the Honda that got hit. The Honda had been stopped
behind me for at least 10-15 seconds when I heard the crash. The impact was pretty severe - loud bang
and the Honda got pushed up close to my bumper."

title: INITIAL EXAMINATION - March 16, 2024
text:
Chief Complaint: Patient presents with severe lower back pain, neck stiffness, and right shoulder pain
following motor vehicle accident on March 15, 2024.
History of Present Illness: Mr. Smith was the driver of a vehicle that was rear-ended at approximately

title: 3:30 PM while stopped at a traffic light on Main Street. Patient reports immediate onset of pain in lower
text:
lumbar region (8/10 severity), cervical spine stiffness, and sharp pain in right shoulder. No loss of
consciousness reported. Patient was transported to Emergency Department by ambulance.
Physical Examination:
Vital Signs: BP 140/85, HR 88, Temp 98.6°F
Neurological: Alert and oriented x3, no focal deficits
Musculoskeletal:
Lumbar spine: Tenderness L3-L5, limited range of motion
Cervical spine: Muscle spasm, restricted rotation
Right shoulder: Pain with abduction, tenderness over AC joint
Assessment:
1. Lumbar strain/sprain secondary to MVA
2. Cervical whiplash injury
3. Right shoulder contusion
Plan:
MRI lumbar spine to rule out disc injury
Physical therapy referral
Muscle relaxants: Flexeril 10mg TID
Anti-inflammatory: Ibuprofen 600mg BID
Work restrictions: No lifting >10 lbs, limited sitting
Follow-up in 2 weeks
Work Status: Unable to return to work as construction supervisor. Estimated duration: 6-8 weeks
minimum.

title: FOLLOW-UP VISIT - March 30, 2024
text:
Subjective: Patient reports persistent lower back pain (7/10), improved neck stiffness, ongoing right
shoulder discomfort. Sleep disruption due to pain. Unable to perform normal work duties.
Objective:
Lumbar spine: Still tender L4-L5, some improvement in ROM
Cervical spine: Reduced muscle spasm
Right shoulder: Persistent tenderness, limited overhead motion
MRI Results (March 25, 2024): Lumbar spine shows mild disc bulge L4-L5 with no nerve root
compression. Consistent with traumatic injury.
Assessment: Improving but persistent post-traumatic musculoskeletal injuries
Plan:
Continue physical therapy 3x/week
Add Gabapentin 300mg for nerve-related pain
Extend work restrictions another 4 weeks
Consider epidural steroid injection if no improvement
Total Medical Expenses to Date: $3,250

title: FOLLOW-UP VISIT - April 20, 2024

Objective:
Lumbar spine: Improved ROM, minimal tenderness
